prompt_text: waist-high editorial industrial photograph of a program buyer curating reusable decision assets on a project table, separating durable governance artifacts, comparison packets, and scorecard logic from old plant-specific snapshot materials; the scene should clearly distinguish reusable structure from one-off historical state through physical folders, clips, and trays rather than screen templates or document text. no readable text, no logos, no brand names, no fake dashboards, no staged stock-photo poses, no sci-fi UI, no over-clean symmetry. Target aspect ratio: 16:9 Critical render rule: do not generate any readable text, letters, numbers, captions, labels, logos, watermarks, slide titles, document copy, dashboard copy, UI text, headline text, wall text, or typographic overlays anywhere in the image. If a screen, board, document, dashboard, scorecard, or interface is visible, it must contain only abstract non-readable blocks, simple shapes, and soft placeholder marks. Never place large title words, marketing slogans, section headers, or composited text for later overlay; leave that area visually quiet and empty instead. Use environmental storytelling and people, not presentation slides or readable screens.
negative_prompt: messy paper storm stock, laptop template screen, copy-paste collage, readable folder labels, office admin flatlay.
alt_text_en: show that buyers should reuse decision logic and proof structures from the last automation project, not blindly copy old project snapshots.
caption_en: show that buyers should reuse decision logic and proof structures from the last automation project, not blindly copy old project snapshots.
